test.name: Golden Config: router backups are in Gitea and every compliance row is compliant
test.status: Test execution stopped due to a fatal error.

suite.doc: The IPsec lab as modelled in the shared Nautobot: devices match the routers, p2p links are cabled, the VPN lives in the core VPN app (VPN, tunnels, hub/spoke endpoints, profile with Phase 1/2 policies), eBGP peerings match the live sessions, the rendered NAC device model matches the committed file, Golden Config is compliant.

suite.name: 07 Firewalls

test.name: Each headend has exactly one firewall, reachable over the OOB network with SSH
test.status: Test execution stopped due to a fatal error.

test.name: Firewall interfaces carry the modelled addresses and face the right neighbours
test.status: Test execution stopped due to a fatal error.

test.name: The rendered firewall configuration matches what runs on the firewalls
test.status: Test execution stopped due to a fatal error.

test.name: Only IKEv2, ESP and ICMP cross the firewall; the tunnels actually carry ESP through it
test.status: Test execution stopped due to a fatal error.

test.name: Firewall bandwidth is modelled in Nautobot and bounds the headend capacity together with the tunnel count
test.doc: Every firewall carries custom field firewall_bandwidth_mbps (from the intent); the VPN records the per-tunnel commitment; the portal's inventory reports both constraints per headend and the aggregate is the tighter of the two.
test.status: Test execution stopped due to a fatal error.

test.name: Headend CPU is collected live and joins the aggregate capacity
test.doc: The portal reads `show platform resources` on every headend: control-plane CPU against the platform's warning threshold, data-plane (QFP) CPU and DRAM. Aggregate utilisation is the tightest of tunnels, bandwidth and CPU.
test.status: Test execution stopped due to a fatal error.

test.name: Non-VPN traffic from a spoke to a headend is dropped by the firewall
test.status: Test execution stopped due to a fatal error.

suite.doc: The VyOS firewall in front of each headend: modelled in Nautobot, configured from it, and actually filtering: only IKEv2, ESP and ICMP cross between the spokes and the headend; anything else is dropped.
